notes: v61 makes a with-statement COM interface prefix live exactly as long as its statement. Two defects, one cause, both only when the with was NOT the first statement of its begin..end: (1) "with Make.o do begin ... end" released the interface behind Make BEFORE the body ran, so the body worked on a freed object -- present in v59 AND in v60 (measured on the exact published exes under wine64: 5 failing corners); (2) "with Make do begin ... end" leaked the prefix until routine exit in v59, which GOD's 407ef9bb3a (v60) fixed and which stays in. Cause: tblocknode.simplify spliced the with's hidden statement list into the enclosing block, and each spliced piece was then released as a statement of its own. Fix 2df7b40d2a (compiler/nbas.pas, +19 lines): never merge a compiler-built list into a source block. Compiler-binary-only refresh on the v60 tarball tree: no PPU format, RTL or package change, so UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.5 MB bin tarball alone; every bin/ member but ppcx64.exe is byte-identical to v60 and v59. ppcx64.exe is 5054976 bytes for the THIRD release running -- verify by md5, never by size. date: is the compiler's own -iD stamp. VERIFIED on lazdev under wine64 with this exact exe against the v52 units: tests/test/tintfwithprefix1.pp (new, 62 corners) 62/62 at -O- and -O2 where the v60 exe fails 5 and the v59 exe 16; tintfstmttemp1/2 32/32 and 28/28; the x86_64-linux compiler from the same source passed the 1987-test corpus A/B against v60 with the new test as the only (intended) DIFF. HONEST LIMIT: wine is NOT Windows; v59 ran on native Windows (2026-09-17), v60 and v61 have not yet -- GOD's IHolder<> run on real Windows is the sign-off. Full record: dist/RELEASE-v61.txt and dist/win64/staging-v61/VERSION.txt.
